TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents

 
 Aaron J. Li 1 ,
 Weijia Xu 2 ,
 Chandan Singh 2 ,
 Zixiao Chen 3 ,
 Jeevana Priya Inala 2 ,
 Charlotte Siska 3 ,
 
 Acar Tamersoy 3 ,
 Bin Yu 1 ,
 Ion Stoica 1 ,
 Michel Galley 2 ,
 Jianfeng Gao 2 
 
 
 1 UC Berkeley   2 Microsoft Research   3 Microsoft Security
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 
 Our measurement on SWE-Bench tasks: 18.4–30.9% lower mean cost across five agent–model
 combinations, cheaper in all 30 repository × combination cells, and Pass@1 up in
 4 of 5 . Results 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

TokenEconomizer makes coding agents cheaper to run in the repositories you work in often,
without changing the agent itself. It learns from the sessions an agent has already run in a
repository, and uses that experience to cut waste in the sessions that follow. It has three
mechanisms:

- Micro-skills: remember how the repository works. Sessions keep rediscovering the same
 facts: a build step that must run first, the spelling of a command that works here
 ( python -m pytest where pytest is missing, npx tsc where tsc is), an environment
 variable a command needs, where generated files live. Micro-skills learns such facts, in any
 language, from two sources: failures that repeat across sessions, and a model that reviews the
 recent sessions every k sessions ( k = 3) and proposes facts. A fact is stated at the start
 of each session once three sessions have confirmed it, and dropped when later sessions
 contradict it.
- Tool pruning: stop loading tools that go unused. Every loaded tool's definition is sent with
 every request. A tool that goes unused over p prompts spread across at least m sessions, or
 over s sessions of any length ( p = 10, m = 2, s = 5), is left out of the next sessions
 through the agent's own settings. One command brings it back.
- Failure-loop intervention (the loop guard): step in when a turn is stuck. When a turn (the
 agent's work on one prompt) keeps hitting the same failures, a judge model checks whether it is
 stuck. If the judge is at least c sure ( c = 0.7), the agent gets a redirect (a short note,
 added to its context, to try another approach), at most r times per turn ( r = 1). If the
 turn is still stuck after that, TokenEconomizer tells you how to stop it; it never stops a turn
 itself.

TokenEconomizer is a plugin for Claude Code , Codex , the GitHub Copilot CLI and Pi ,
with experimental support for opencode , Cursor Agent , Grok Build , Hermes Agent ,
the Antigravity CLI and Factory Droid . Each italic
letter above is a setting, shown with its default (Settings), and each mechanism can be turned on or
off. The plugin announces each action in one line, and if any part of it fails, your session
carries on as if it were not installed. Its model calls (the fact proposer, and the judge with the
redirect it writes) run through your own agent, on the same plan or login, and their cost is
included in its reports. What it learns stays on your machine, in /.tokeneconomizer .

 Results

The paper ran five agent–model combinations on the same 277 SWE-Bench tasks from six repositories.
Each task ran as its own session, and each repository's tasks ran in order, starting with nothing
learned. Costs include every model call TokenEconomizer made. Within each repository and
combination, cost fell by 5–40%. The savings held on Web-Bench (16–21% lower) and on two
security-auditing benchmarks where every task is in a new repository (6–20% lower). The
project page has interactive charts, per-repository numbers
and nine annotated runs, and experiments/ reruns the SWE-Bench and
Web-Bench experiments.

 How it works

 

Coding agents are built to finish tasks, not to keep them cheap. Every turn pays again for the
agent's instructions, every loaded tool, and the conversation so far. Developers use the same
agent on the same repository again and again, so much of that cost repeats: the same facts
rediscovered, the same unused tools sent, the same kinds of failing loops. TokenEconomizer leaves
the agent's model, weights and code alone and learns across a repository's sessions instead of
treating each one on its own, so whatever the plugin spends is paid back over the sessions that
follow. Four principles guide the mechanisms:

- Work through what the agent already reads. Facts enter the context at session start, and
 tools are removed through the agent's own settings, so nothing depends on the agent learning a
 new tool.
- Count cost as it is billed. Most tokens in a session are cached re-reads, so cost is
 computed with cache pricing, and it includes the plugin's own model calls.
- Protect task success. Facts form only from repeated evidence, tools are removed only after
 going unused, and the loop guard leaves alone a turn that is still making progress.
- Keep every action reversible. A fact that later sessions contradict is dropped, removed
 tools can be given back, and the loop guard only redirects and tells you: stopping a turn is
 your call.

 Quick start

You need one of these agents, signed in any way it supports, and Python 3.10 or newer on
 PATH . The plugin needs no API key of its own and never handles credentials, so any plan or
login works.

 Install

Run these commands in the folder where you want to keep the clone. Claude Code, Codex, the
Copilot CLI and opencode run the plugin from the clone, so leave it in place. Then start the agent
in one of your repositories.

 Claude Code 

 

Start claude , trust the folder ( Yes, I trust this folder ), and run
 /tokeneconomizer:status , allowing its script if asked. Once per machine, and again after Claude
Code updates, run /tokeneconomizer:toolprune refresh-catalog .

 Codex 

 

Start codex , choose Trust and continue for the folder, then at Hooks need review 
choose Trust all and continue . The hooks take effect from your next Codex session, so quit
( /exit ), start codex again, and check with $tokeneconomizer:status .

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
You need one of these agents, signed in any way it supports, and Python 3.10 or newer on PATH. The plugin needs no API key of its own and never handles credentials, so any plan or login works.

Install

Run these commands in the folder where you want to keep the clone. Claude Code, Codex, the Copilot CLI and opencode run the plugin from the clone, so leave it in place. Then start the agent in one of your repositories.

Claude Code

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"
claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer

Start claude, trust the folder (Yes, I trust this folder), and run /tokeneconomizer:status, allowing its script if asked. Once per machine, and again after Claude Code updates, run /tokeneconomizer:toolprune refresh-catalog.

Codex

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"
codex plugin add tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer

Start codex, choose Trust and continue for the folder, then at Hooks need review choose Trust all and continue. The hooks take effect from your next Codex session, so quit (/exit), start codex again, and check with $tokeneconomizer:status.

Copilot CLI

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
copilot plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"
copilot plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer

Start copilot, choose Yes, and remember this folder for future sessions, and run /tokeneconomizer:status, choosing Yes to run its script. Once per machine, and again after Copilot updates, run /tokeneconomizer:toolprune refresh-catalog.

Pi

pi install git:github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer

Start pi and run /te status.

Factory Droid (experimental; micro-skills, the loop guard and session cost, not tool pruning)

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
cd TokenEconomizer
python scripts/build_plugin.py --droid
droid plugin marketplace add "$PWD/dist/tokeneconomizer-droid"
droid plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer-droid --scope user

Start a new Droid session (its hooks are snapshotted at startup) and run /tokeneconomizer-status. Droid keeps each session's token usage in a settings file beside its log, so folded sessions are priced like any other host's. Its TUI has no persistent per-tool setting, so tool pruning stays off; and because droid exec writes a session log of its own, micro-skills' paid proposer and the loop guard's judge stay off until droid_sidecall is on (when on, they may use only Droid's read-only Read tool). See docs/DROID.md for what works and how to import earlier sessions.

Cursor Agent (experimental)

python scripts/build_plugin.py --out ~/.cursor/plugins/local/

Reload Cursor, confirm tokeneconomizer appears in Customize, then send a prompt in a repository. Check its state from a terminal with ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te --host cursor status. Cursor's published hooks provide session, prompt, tool-result and completion events. Its transcript format and per-session token usage are not a supported public interface, so the adapter records needed hook events locally and reports session cost as unavailable. Cursor support is macOS and Linux only: on Windows, Cursor runs hook commands through PowerShell, and this plugin's launcher is a POSIX shell script.

Grok Build (experimental)

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
grok plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"
grok plugin install tokeneconomizer --trust

Grok runs Claude Code plugins, so this is the Claude Code plugin: grok loads plugin/hooks/hooks.json and TokenEconomizer recognises the grok session in the hook payload. (If you already installed it for Claude Code, grok reads ~/.claude/plugins and runs it in your sessions; this version reads those as grok sessions.) Micro-skills and the loop guard only; tool pruning is not available. Confirm tokeneconomizer is enabled in grok plugin list, start grok, and check with ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te --host grok status. The learned facts arrive with the session's first tool call, not at its start (its limits).

Antigravity CLI (agy; experimental; micro-skills' LLM-free facts only)

python scripts/build_plugin.py --out dist/marketplace
agy plugin install dist/marketplace/tokeneconomizer

Start agy and send a prompt in a repository, then check with ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te --host antigravity status (on Windows, <plugin>\scripts\te.cmd --host antigravity status, run in the repository; <plugin> is the folder above scripts\te_bootstrap.py in %USERPROFILE%\.tokeneconomizer\bin\te.json, which the first session writes). agy has no plugin commands, so the plugin's commands run from a terminal. The plugin makes no model call through agy, which has no option that runs a prompt with every tool off, so the paid proposer and the loop guard are off and tool pruning is not available. Works across Windows, macOS, and Linux with native Windows batch launchers (scripts\te-hook.cmd, scripts\te.cmd). Tested on agy 1.5.1 and 1.5.2 on Windows 11, macOS, and Linux. See its limits.

opencode (experimental)

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
ln -s "$PWD/TokenEconomizer/plugin/opencode/tokeneconomizer.ts" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/

The one file serves both generations: opencode 1.x reads its server entry, 2.x its setup. Start opencode and send a prompt, then check in the repository with ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te --host opencode status. opencode has no plugin commands, so the plugin's commands run from a terminal.

Hermes Agent (experimental; micro-skills and the loop guard, on the classic CLI and one-shot runs)

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git
ln -s "$PWD/TokenEconomizer/plugin/hermes" ~/.hermes/plugins/tokeneconomizer
hermes plugins enable tokeneconomizer
hermes gateway restart

Link it rather than running hermes plugins install, which leaves the launchers behind when given this directory and refuses the whole repository at its security scan. Send a prompt, then check in the repository with ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te --host hermes status.

If the install worked, the status command prints a short status block. refresh-catalog records every tool a session loads (without a model call), so that tool pruning can consider all of them. Keep the marketplace path absolute, as above: the Copilot CLI reads a relative path such as ./TokenEconomizer as the name of a GitHub repository.

To update:

Agent Update
Claude Code, Copilot CLI, opencode git pull in the clone
Factory Droid git pull in the clone, then the build_plugin.py --droid and install lines again
Hermes Agent git pull in the clone, then hermes gateway restart
Antigravity CLI build the bundle again and agy plugin install it
Codex git pull in the clone, then the codex plugin add line again
Pi pi update --extensions

plugin/README.md walks through each agent in more detail, including uninstalling, using Copilot with your own model key, and troubleshooting.

Agent Supported Older versions

Codex 0.153.1 to 0.164.0 not supported
Copilot CLI 1.0.83 to 1.0.102 not supported
Pi 1.2.0 to 1.3.0 0.99.x: load the extension by path (below)
Cursor Agent (experimental) 3.24.9 and cursor-agent 2026.11.05, macOS and Linux (below) not tested
Grok Build (experimental) 1.0.70 not tested
opencode (experimental) 1.19.5 and 2.2.0 not tested
Hermes Agent (experimental) 0.22.5 not tested
Antigravity CLI (experimental) agy 1.5.1 and 1.5.2, Windows 11, macOS and Linux not tested
Factory Droid (experimental) 0.233.0, macOS (below) not tested

The commands above were tested on the oldest and newest version in each range; newer versions have not been tested yet.
